testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you are not sure how to put out a fire in your vehicle, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you don't know what type of fire extinguisher to use, especially for dangerous materials, wait for the firefighters to arrive. Let them handle the fire.

questions.question: What happens if you have more than one license?

options.text: You are unlikely to be caught.
There is no way for authorities to find out.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one license. Breaking this law can result in jail time and/or a fine up to $5,000.

questions.question: After being convicted of a traffic violation, when must you tell your employer?
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer within 30 days of any traffic violation conviction. You must also tell your motor vehicle agency within 30 days if the violation happened in another state. Parking tickets do not require notification.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a vehicle inspection?

options.text: The inspection report is not important.
The inspection report only matters if passengers will be in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report, if one exists.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report, if one exists.
questions.explanation: Start by reviewing the last inspection report. Only sign the new report after confirming that any problems found before have been fixed.

questions.question: What task may a CDL applicant be asked to do during the vehicle inspection test?
questions.explanation: The CDL vehicle inspection test includes a full inspection. You will be required to check the engine oil level.

questions.question: When does antifreeze help keep an engine working properly?

options.text: Only when it is cold outside.
To make the vehicle more fuel efficient.
In both cold and hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: In both cold and hot weather.
questions.explanation: Always keep enough water and antifreeze in your cooling system. Despite its name, antifreeze is important even in hot weather.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of a road in winter?

options.text: They don't get moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sun and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery even after ice on other parts of the road has melted.

questions.question: If you are driving so slowly that you will slow down other drivers, what should you do?
questions.explanation: If you must drive slowly and slow down traffic, turn on your four-way flashers to warn drivers behind you (if local laws allow).

questions.question: When turning left at an intersection with two left turn lanes, which lane should you use?

options.text: It doesn't matter which lane you use.

questions.explanation: You may need to swing right before turning left. Always start your turn in the rightmost left turn lane when two left turn lanes are available.

questions.question: What is required to transport hanging meat in a refrigerated truck?

options.text: It is good experience for new drivers.
It is illegal in most states.

questions.explanation: Transporting hanging meat requires careful driving. The load is unstable because it sits high and swings around, which affects how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: Front tires must have a tread depth of ____ in every major groove.
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need 4/32 of an inch tread depth on front tires and 2/32 of an inch on other tires for safe operation.

questions.question: During a vehicle inspection, which item do you NOT need to check?

options.text: That the oil pressure gauge is working.
That the oil pressure warning light turns off, or that the gauge shows normal oil pressure.
That the oil temperature gauge, if equipped, rises to normal operating temperature.
That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.

questions.correctAnswerText: That the oil pressure gauge comes on when brakes are used.
questions.explanation: Check that the oil pressure gauge works and shows normal pressure or that the warning light turns off. If equipped, the oil temperature gauge should rise to normal operating temperature. The oil pressure gauge should not come on when you use the brakes.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk when it is hard to see your vehicle, you can help other drivers by:

options.text: Waving an arm out the window.

questions.explanation: When you have trouble seeing others, they have trouble seeing you. Turn on your headlights to low beam when visibility is low.

questions.question: At dawn or dusk, you can make your vehicle easier to see by:
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dawn, dusk, and in snow or rain so other drivers can see your vehicle.

questions.question: What are placards?

options.text: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards
A type of tire used in snowy conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: Signs placed on a vehicle to identify cargo hazards
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped warning signs placed on the outside of vehicles carrying hazardous materials. They identify the type of hazard in the cargo.

questions.question: A vehicle's center of gravity height:

options.text: Usually has no impact on vehicle handling.
Plays a large role in how safely you can handle the vehicle.
Should not be a concern when loading.
Should only matter if the route has many hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plays a large role in how safely you can handle the vehicle.
questions.explanation: A vehicle's center of gravity height is very important for safe handling. Keep cargo weight as low as possible.

questions.question: ABS brakes:

options.text: Prevent your vehicle from accelerating uphill.

questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When driving downhill, your vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls your vehicle downhill and causes your speed to increase.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, you should:

options.text: Activate your hazard lights and continue driving.
Call the local law enforcement agency.
Safely exit the roadway and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely exit the roadway and stop.
questions.explanation: Stop immediately and park safely when the air pressure warning light comes on. This warning means there is a problem with the air brake system that needs to be fixed.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, warning lights and buzzers:

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until you turn them off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After starting the engine, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging, and ABS should turn off right away.

questions.question: Why should you perform pre-trip inspection steps in the same order each time?

options.text: You will be less likely to forget something.
You will have more time to complete the inspection.

questions.correctAnswerText: You will be less likely to forget something.
questions.explanation: Using the same order every time helps you remember all the steps. Following a set checklist makes it less likely you will skip something.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle gets stuck on railroad tracks?

options.text: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
Keep trying to get your vehicle off the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the vehicle and call for help.
questions.explanation: Leave your vehicle immediately and move away from the tracks. Look for emergency contact information on signs at the crossing. Call 911 or another emergency number.

questions.question: To avoid a hazard, you:

options.text: Should always steer to the left.
May be able to drive onto the shoulder.
Should steer sharply in one direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: May be able to drive onto the shoulder.
questions.explanation: In an emergency, driving onto the shoulder may be the best way to avoid a hazard. Most shoulders are strong enough to support a large vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: Get away from the aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact, do not speed up to challenge them, and do not react to angry gestures.

questions.question: Loading weight with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
Increases the likelihood that items will fall down.
Increases the difficulty of unloading the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the likelihood of a rollover.
questions.explanation: A high center of gravity makes the vehicle more likely to tip over. Cargo should be loaded with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: Near a railroad crossing:

options.text: You will hear every approaching train.
You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
You will hear two short blasts if a train is approaching.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not hear a train, even if one is approaching.
questions.explanation: Never assume you will hear a train. The operator may not sound the horn, or horns may be prohibited in that area. Noise inside your vehicle may block the sound of a train until it is dangerously close.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system:

options.text: Air tanks are shared between both systems.
Each system has its own air tanks.
You must choose which system you are using.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own air tanks.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate systems. They share the brake controls, but each system has its own tanks, hoses, and lines.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that spring brakes come on when:
questions.explanation: Spring brakes should come on automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Block the wheels and release air by stepping on and off the brake pedal. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve should pop out and spring brakes should engage.

questions.question: The brake pedal is part of which brake system?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is controlled by the brake pedal. It applies and releases brakes during normal driving.

questions.question: When entering a curve, you should:
questions.explanation: Slow down to a safe speed and shift into a lower gear before entering a curve.

questions.question: Which is NOT a reason to cover cargo?

options.text: To protect people if cargo spills

questions.explanation: Cover cargo to protect people from spilled cargo and to protect the cargo from weather.

questions.question: When should cargo be checked?

options.text: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
Only by the people who load it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before the trip and again within the first 50 miles.
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles after that. Also check it each time you stop for a break. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing during a driving test?

options.text: Pass another vehicle if it is moving too slowly.
Change lanes while on the tracks.
Do not change gears while on the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not change gears while on the tracks.
questions.explanation: During a driving test, do not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of your vehicle is on railroad tracks.

questions.question: What should you do if an aggressive driver crashes ahead?

options.text: Pull over and yell at them.
Stop safely and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop safely and tell police about the aggressive driving you saw.
questions.explanation: If you see a crash with an aggressive driver, stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the aggressive behavior you witnessed.

questions.question: Pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can:

options.text: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
Add more air to the brake system.
Make the brake pedal more sensitive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release air faster than it can be replaced.
questions.explanation: In an air brake system, pressing and releasing the brake pedal too many times can release air faster than the compressor can replace it.

questions.question: When are you most likely to encounter strong winds?
questions.explanation: Strong winds make it hard to keep your vehicle in its lane. This is especially true when driving out of a tunnel.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997, and other vehicles with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1998, must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: If mirrors are dirty before you start driving:

options.text: They will clean themselves after driving a short distance.
You do not need to worry about it.

questions.explanation: Before you start, check your mirrors and windshield for dirt or anything blocking your view. Clean them if needed.

questions.question: An open car window in cold weather may mean the driver is:

options.text: Using the heat in their vehicle.

questions.explanation: Watch other drivers for signs they may be impaired. Drivers who drank too much, are tired, used drugs, or are sick are dangerous. A driver with their window open in cold weather may be impaired.

questions.question: What type of brakes do most newer heavy trucks use?
questions.explanation: Most newer heavy trucks use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brakes that share one set of brake controls.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repairs.
Safe if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe to use. You must replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks:

options.text: Usually have low centers of gravity.
Usually have high centers of gravity.
Usually are not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Usually have high centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. Drivers must be careful because the cargo can shift during transport, which changes how the vehicle handles.

questions.question: An air brake-equipped vehicle traveling at 55 mph under ideal conditions needs approximately ____ feet to stop completely.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. At 55 mph under ideal conditions, an air brake-equipped vehicle needs about 450 feet to stop.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board must be secure, undamaged, and strong enough to contain cargo during vehicle inspection.

questions.question: The only way to sober up after drinking alcohol is to:
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Cold showers or coffee will not speed this up. You must allow your body time to eliminate the alcohol.

questions.question: If involved in a crash, basic procedures should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: After a crash, you must protect the area, notify authorities, and help the injured. Never leave the scene. Protecting the area helps prevent another crash in the same spot.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air once air tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when tanks reach 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: A 40-foot load should be secured with at least ____ tie-downs.
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs minimum.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is involved in a crash ahead of you, you should:

options.text: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
Block the driver in with your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at a safe distance, wait for police, and tell them about the driver's behavior.
questions.explanation: Stop at a safe distance from the crash. Wait for police to arrive and inform them of the aggressive behavior you saw.

questions.question: When stopping, the brake pedal:
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal gradually. Control the pressure to bring your vehicle to a slow, safe stop.
